protocol.title: NF-kappaB Memory Coordinates Transcriptional Responses to Dynamic Inflammatory Stimuli
protocol.platform: Automated microfluidic live-cell imaging (channel-based, pressure-driven, PDMS/glass)
cell_lines: RelA^-/- NIH/3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts stably expressing RelA-DsRed, JNK-KTR-mCerulean3, H2B-GFP
protocol.objective: Systematic single-cell profiling of NF-kappaB responses to 24 non-repeating sequential combinations of four inflammatory ligands at three dose levels; information-theoretic quantification of stimulus history encoding; IKK inhibition and transcriptomics to identify ligand-dependent negative feedback mechanisms producing short-term NF-kappaB memory

device.type: Pressure-driven automated microfluidic cell culture device (channel-based, not DMF)
device.design_reference: Kellogg et al. 2014, Nat. Protoc. 9, 1713; Son et al. 2021, Sci. Signal. 14, eaaz4382
device.fabrication: Multilayer soft lithography; control layer 66 g PDMS poured on silicon wafer, cured 80 C overnight; flow layer 15 g PDMS spun at 2200 rpm (50 um thick), cured 80 C 1 h; bonded by oxygen plasma alignment and 80 C overnight bake
device.surface_coating: 0.25 mg/mL human plasma fibronectin (Millipore) in sterile PBS pH 7.4; overnight at room temperature
device.control: Pneumatic solenoid valves driven by MATLAB scripts + custom GUI; input pressure 4 psi; PEEK tubing (VICI TPK.505) reagent delivery
device.microscope: Nikon Ti2 enclosed in temperature-controlled incubator (Life Imaging Services)

reagents.cell_culture_medium: DMEM High Glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 1% GlutaMAX (Gibco) + 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin (Gibco)
reagents.imaging_medium: FluoroBrite DMEM (Gibco, A1896701) + same supplements; used to reduce background fluorescence during live imaging
reagents.surface_coating: Human plasma fibronectin 0.25 mg/mL in PBS (Gibco)

doses.mid: 30 ng/mL  (85-95% cells activated; maximal TNF-alpha activation ~90%)

LPS.full_name: Ultrapure LPS from E. coli 0111:B4 (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps)
LPS.pathway: MyD88 -> IRAK1/4 -> IKK -> NF-kappaB (MyD88-dependent; TRIF/TRAM pathway negligible in 3T3s)

IKK_inhibitor.name: PS1145 dihydrochloride (Tocris, 4569)
IKK_inhibitor.notes: Washed out after LPS stimulus (2x15 min complete media washes) before IL-1beta restimulation

antibodies_western.MyD88: Cell Signaling Technologies, D80F5 Rabbit mAb, Cat. 4283 (1:1000)

stimulus_design.description: 24 non-repeating permutations of 4 ligands (T, I, L, P) at each of 3 dose levels = 72 total conditions; 1 positive control (mid-dose T-I-L-P), 1 negative control (4x complete media); each condition analyzed in 2 independent biological replicates
stimulus_design.normalization: Single-cell responses normalized to mean S1 response for the corresponding ligand at each dose

information_theory.method: Channel capacity (CC) = max mutual information I(R;S) over input probability distribution Q
information_theory.features: Nuclear NF-kappaB amplitude at 6 timepoints per stimulus interval (20, 30, 40, 50, 70, 90 min post-stimulus)

steps.name: Device fabrication and surface coating
steps.notes: PDMS device bonded to glass slide by oxygen plasma. Chambers filled with 0.25 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS, incubated overnight at room temperature. Chambers flushed with complete medium before cell loading.

steps.name: Cell loading and equilibration
steps.operation: flow-through loading (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: Cells harvested with trypsin, resuspended in FluoroBrite DMEM, loaded at ~50% confluency to optimize tracking efficiency. 5 h equilibration before imaging start.

steps.name: S1 stimulus - naive NF-kappaB response
steps.operation: automated ligand delivery via MATLAB valve control
steps.notes: Naive response: no prior inflammatory ligand exposure. S1 response used as baseline for normalization of S2-S4 responses. Ligand diluted from -80 C stock immediately before stimulus; stored on ice during experiment.

steps.name: S1 QC gate - valid naive response check
steps.notes: Cells with no detectable S1 response excluded from analysis. 95th percentile of maxima from unstimulated cells used as cutoff threshold.

steps.name: S2 stimulus - first history-conditioned response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: Prior IL-1beta (S1) induces MyD88-dependent IRAK1 auto-inhibition attenuating LPS response at mid dose (Fig. 4B/E). Channel capacity increases from S1 to S2, encoding prior history (Fig. 3B).

steps.name: S3 stimulus - two-ligand history response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: Cumulative MyD88-dependent history (IL-1beta + LPS) induces downstream NF-kappaB-dependent negative feedback (A20, IkappaBepsilon upregulation). CC remains elevated at S3 vs S1 (Fig. 3B/C).

steps.name: S4 stimulus - three-ligand history response
steps.operation: automated ligand switch via MATLAB valve control
steps.key_finding: TNF-alpha signals via TNFR (not MyD88), bypassing accumulated IRAK1 auto-inhibition and downstream MyD88-dependent feedbacks from S1-S3. TNF-alpha response only weakly attenuated regardless of prior history (Figs. 2B, 4B/D).

pass.action: cell retrieval for RNA-seq; continue to IKK sub-protocol

steps.name: Cell retrieval for transcriptomics (S4 pass path only)
steps.library_prep: SMART-Seq2 (modified); TSO oligo AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTGAAT[rG][rG][rG]; OligodT30VN; 6 cycles KAPA HiFi preamplification; Nextera XT library prep
steps.sequencing: Illumina HiSEQ4000; single-end 50 bp; University of Chicago Genomics Facility
steps.alignment: STAR; reference GRCm38; transcript quantification by featureCounts
steps.differential_expression: R packages edgeR + limma; BH FDR < 0.01 and log2FC > 1

steps.name: IKK inhibition sub-protocol (Fig. 5A)
steps.purpose: Test whether NF-kappaB signalling downstream of IKK is required for LPS-dependent attenuation of subsequent IL-1beta responses
steps.operation: PS1145 pretreatment -> LPS stimulus -> wash -> IL-1beta rechallenge

substeps.name: PS1145 pretreatment
substeps.reagent: PS1145 dihydrochloride 40 uM in complete media

substeps.name: LPS + PS1145 co-stimulus
substeps.reagent: LPS (25-400 ng/mL) + 40 uM PS1145 in complete media
substeps.notes: NF-kappaB translocation significantly reduced during LPS stimulus due to IKK-beta inhibition (Supp. Fig. 6D)

substeps.name: IL-1beta rechallenge
substeps.result: PS1145-treated cells show significantly stronger NF-kappaB response vs untreated (***p < 1e-4); >120 cells per condition, 2 biological replicates (Fig. 5A)

negative_feedback_model.description: Two-motif ODE model: (1) IRAK1 auto-inhibitory phosphorylation (upstream, shared by all MyD88-dependent ligands); (2) NF-kappaB-dependent downstream inhibitor expression (A20, IkappaBepsilon; LPS-induced 4x stronger than IL-1beta or TNF-alpha)
negative_feedback_model.key_prediction: At high dose: symmetric IRAK1-driven attenuation among all MyD88-dependent ligands. At mid/low dose: asymmetric attenuation - prior LPS inhibits IL-1beta/PAM but not vice versa, due to differential downstream feedback induction.

transcriptomics.condition: Mid-dose 2 h stimulus: LPS (100 ng/mL) vs PAM (0.2 ng/mL) vs IL-1beta (0.2 ng/mL) vs untreated
transcriptomics.conclusion: Differences in NF-kappaB activation duration (not total AUC) drive differential downstream gene expression between LPS and IL-1beta. LPS produces longer NF-kappaB activation duration; 1 ng/mL IL-1beta (matching LPS AUC) does not induce comparable Nfkbia or Tnfaip3 expression.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: Device prep, fibronectin coating, cell loading, 5 h equilibration, S1 IL-1beta-Mid stimulus

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_13_j
basic_blocks.description: IKK sub-protocol: PS1145 pretreat -> LPS 240 m -> 2x wash -> IL-1beta-High rechallenge + detect
